analysis: This batch contains only documentation: an added changelog, changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md (head lines 1-8), and edits to docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head line 3 date bump; line 65 Streaming read row). Both describe a code change in SSDBlockStore.readExactly that keeps a field or chunk in its original read buffer, without a second copy, when one read returns it whole. The Swift source for that change is not in this batch, so this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. Relevant threat: T-041 (DBK3 AES-GCM per-chunk auth, AAD metadata, bounded reads, retry byte budget per base line 278 referencing readExactly). The docs claim no change to authentication, AAD, chunk bounds (maximumChunkBytes), EOF/file-identity checks, or the retry raw-byte ceiling. Integration must verify in SSDBlockStore.swift and SSDBlockChunkCursor.swift: (1) the single-read path still enforces exact length, with no short-read acceptance or oversized buffer; (2) the uncopied Data or slice is not aliased or mutated after authentication, so decryption cannot run on a buffer that a later read overwrites (TOCTOU); (3) SSDCheckpointReadBudget.beforeRead charging is unchanged for the fast path, including partial reads; (4) plaintext and ciphertext buffer lifetime and zeroing posture are unchanged (T-028/T-041 host-memory reservations, base line 126). The docs alone show no security regression.
